en: The amihan brings cool, dry northeast winds to the Philippines between November and February, helping farmers dry their harvested palay.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is a perfect stratovolcano that frequently produces dangerous pyroclastic flows and lava during its eruptions.
Large deposits of chromite, an iron-chromium mineral used to make stainless steel, are mined from the ultramafic rocks of Zambales.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features a navigable underground river that flows directly through a limestone cave system into St. Paul Bay.
The rich volcanic soil surrounding Mayon Volcano in Bicol contains essential minerals that make it highly fertile for growing abaca plants.
Baguio City experiences a cooler climate than Manila because its high elevation in the Cordillera mountains causes the air to expand and cool.
The Marikina Valley Fault System is a major fracture in the Earth's crust that can generate strong earthquakes affecting Metro Manila.
Heavy monsoon rains cause rapid surface runoff that carries eroded soil from the Sierra Madre mountains into the Cagayan River.
The Diwata-2 microsatellite, built by Filipinos, orbits the Earth to capture high-resolution images of typhoons and monitor local crop health.
Traditional Visayan farmers used the Moroporo constellation, the local name for the Pleiades star cluster, to determine the best time for planting rice.
The gravitational pull of the moon creates high and low tides in Manila Bay, which local fisherfolk use to time their fishing trips.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released massive amounts of pumice, a light, porous volcanic rock that sometimes floats on water.
